title: Chicken and Dumplings
subtitle: Post-shift hug in a pot
description: Post-shift hug in a pot. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Chicken and Dumplings in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use Carrots, diced, Celery, diced, Fresh parsley, chopped as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Sear aromatics
steps.instruction: Brown meat in batches; remove. Sweat onion, carrot, celery in the same pot 8 minutes until edges soften. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Simmer the broth
steps.instruction: Return chicken to the pot with broth and vegetables. Simmer 35 minutes until chicken is tender; shred meat and return to the pot. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Drop the dumplings
steps.instruction: Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt. Cut in butter, then stir in milk and eggs until a thick batter forms. Drop spoonfuls onto simmering broth, cover, and cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Chicken and Dumplings onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Ladle and garnish
steps.instruction: Dumplings should be puffed and cooked through — a skewer should come out clean. Stir in parsley and serve hot from the pot. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Keep the pot on low simmer on the stove — ladle from the side so the bottom doesn't scorch.
Set shredded cheese, crackers, and hot sauce in a row beside the pot.
Line up Chicken and Dumplings on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Post-shift hug in a pot. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
Ground turkey swaps 1:1 for beef in chili if the crew wants leaner.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Chicken and Dumplings runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
